name: Nar Phu Valley Trek
alt_names: Nar Phu and Kang La Pass Trek
sub_region: Manang District, Gandaki Province (Narpa Bhumi Rural Municipality; Annapurna Conservation Area, restricted area)

difficulty.notes: Remote restricted-area trek with sleeping altitudes above 4,000 m at Phu and Nar and a long Kang La (5,320 m) crossing to Ngawal (8-9 h, steep knee-heavy descent). Koto-Meta is a ~960 m sleeping-altitude gain. [s5][s6][s7]

duration_days.basis: full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu, exiting by jeep from Manang
duration_days.notes: Many itineraries continue from Ngawal/Manang over Thorong La to Muktinath and Jomsom (16-19 days). Some add a Kang La Phedi (4,530 m) camp or an extra rest day at Nar. [s7][s8]

start_point: Koto (2,600 m), reached by jeep via Besisahar

itinerary.notes: Agency applies for restricted area permit.
Nearly 1,000 m gain through the Phu Khola gorge. [s6][s7]
Entered through a kani gateway; Tashi Lhakhang monastery. [s6][s7]

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation day in Phu (Tashi Lhakhang; hike toward Himlung viewpoint ~4,400 m)

itinerary.notes: Start before first light; turn back if the pass has heavy fresh snow. [s6][s7]

best_seasons.notes: Upper Marsyangdi road can close in heavy monsoon rain. [s7] RAP fee is higher Sep-Nov. [s3]

permits.name: Nar Phu Restricted Area Permit (Department of Immigration)
permits.fee: Sep-Nov: USD 100 per person for first week + USD 15 per day beyond; Dec-Aug: USD 75 per person for first week + USD 15 per day beyond (NTB table). DoI services page lists USD 90 (Sep-Nov) / USD 75 (Dec-Aug).

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per foreign national (SAARC NPR 1,000), tax included

guide_requirements: Restricted area: permit only via a registered trekking agency with a licensed guide throughout. Since 22 March 2026 solo trekkers may obtain the permit (previously minimum two); max seven trekkers per guide. [s9][s10] NTB lists 'Nar Phu Annapurna Circuit Trek' under the mandatory-guide rule. [s11]

flights: Optional exit Jomsom - Pokhara ~20-25 min if continuing over Thorong La [s8][s12]
drives: Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani/Koto 8-10 h; jeep can reach Koto in one long day [s6][s7]
logistics.notes: Basic lodges at Meta, Kyang, Phu, Nar Phedi and Nar; Kang La Phedi stage, if used, may require camping. [s7]

highlights: Medieval stone villages of Phu and Nar [s6]
Tashi Lhakhang monastery in Phu and Satek Gompa at Nar Phedi [s6]
Kang La (5,320 m) panorama of Annapurna II, III, IV and Gangapurna [s7]
Phu Khola gorge, canyons and kani gateways [s6]
Few trekkers due to restricted status [s6]
risks: Kang La snow; long exposed pass day [s7]
Monsoon road closures on the Marsyangdi road [s7]

acclimatization.notes: Rest day at Phu standard; optional second rest day at Nar before Kang La. [s5][s7]

unverified: Nar Phu RAP peak-season fee: NTB lists USD 100/week (Sep-Nov) while the DoI services page lists USD 90; off-season USD 75/week and USD 15/day beyond the first week agree.
Kang La altitude is given as 5,306-5,322 m in operator sources; 5,320 m is most common.
Nar altitude 4,110-4,205 m depending on source.
